title: Use the parent sign
summary: The ampersand sign stands for the selector around it.
introduction: The ampersand sign stands for the selector around it. Your task: Change the focus outline to a different visible colour.
learningObjectives: Change the focus outline to a different visible colour.
Explain the example for use the parent sign

blocks.text: The ampersand sign stands for the selector around it. It is useful when the same element changes state, such as a button being focused.
Use Dart Sass on your computer. Install Node.js first, with help if needed. Save SCSS examples as lesson.scss and run npx sass lesson.scss lesson.css. This site does not compile Sass.
Read the code step by step

items: `:focus-visible` selects a control when the browser decides its focus should be shown, commonly during keyboard use.
`outline` draws a visible line around the control. In a value such as `3px solid navy`, the parts mean thickness, line style and colour.

blocks.text: Sass creates .button:focus-visible. A keyboard user can see a clear outline when the button receives focus.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: Without &, a nested :focus-visible would choose a focused child instead of the button itself.

blocks.title: Your small task
blocks.text: Change the focus outline to a different visible colour.
